item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning no. Abiy’s 2024 government did back several targeted inclusion and reconstruction programs for girls, refugees, IDPs, women, and disadvantaged regions, but the year also featured severe conflict harm, displacement, aid diversion, emergency repression, and weak protection for vulnerable civilians. The positive record is real but mostly programmatic; the negative record is operational and broader.

**Positive Evidence**
- **[Breaking Barriers: Empowering Girls with Clean Water and Sanitation Facilities in Ethiopia's Schools](/worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/01/19/breaking-barriers-empowering-girls-with-clean-water-and-sanitation-facilities-in-ethiopias-schools)** | World Bank | 2024-01-19 | Over 5,000 schools received WASH facilities and 223 menstrual-hygiene rooms, with attendance gains especially for girls. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`
- **[Bringing Back More Schools, Health Facilities & Life in Tigray](/ethiopia.un.org/en/261479-bringing-back-more-schools-health-facilities-life-tigray)** | United Nations in Ethiopia | 2024-02-23 | Reconstructed 14 health centers, 11 schools, and 33 WASH facilities for 365,000 people in five woredas, which is direct reconstruction in a war-affected marginalized region. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`
- **[Second Phase of PROSPECTS Launched in Ethiopia, Empowering Refugees, IDPs and Host Communities](/unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/second-phase-prospects-launched-ethiopia-empowering-refugees-idps-and-host)** | UNICEF Ethiopia | 2024-03-21 | The partnership focused on education, livelihoods, protection, and infrastructure for refugees, IDPs, and host communities. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`
- **[Ethiopia signs 1.72 billion USD Financing Agreements with the World Bank](/mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/)** | Ministry of Finance, Ethiopia | 2024-04-05 | Funding targeted rural connectivity, food security, adaptive safety nets, and other public-good projects aimed at inclusive growth. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **[Building a Strong Foundation to Improve Learning Outcomes in Ethiopia](/worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia)** | World Bank | 2024-09-05 | The education program trained 102,117 teachers and reported improved girls’ enrollment and refugee-school support in disadvantaged regions. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **[Ethiopia's health-financing progress](/ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5233579)** | ENA English | 2024-10-03 | The ministry said health insurance coverage improved and barriers to primary care fell, which is favorable for poor households and vulnerable patients. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`
- **[Ethiopia Considers Social Protection as Core Component of National Dev’t: Minister](/ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5452428)** | ENA English | 2024-11-13 | Social protection was explicitly described as central policy, signaling stated priority for vulnerable households. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`
- **[Social Welfare Key Pillar of Prime Ministerial Initiatives](/ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4920073)** | ENA English | 2024-08-05 | The PM office framed housing support for the elderly and economically vulnerable as an ongoing initiative. | `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `6B.2`

**Negative Evidence**
- **[World Report 2024: Ethiopia](/hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-12 | Aid diversion led WFP and USAID to halt food aid, sharply restricting access for about 20 million people, especially in displacement and refugee camps. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **[Ethiopia Military Executes Dozens of Civilians in Amhara Region](/hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-04 | Federal forces allegedly killed dozens of civilians, showing vulnerable civilians were not protected as a governing priority in conflict zones. | `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.9`
- **[Ethiopia: Army Attacks Health Care in Amhara Conflict](/hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-03 | Security forces attacked ambulances, hospitals, and medical staff, directly harming access to care for wounded and civilians. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.9`
- **[Nearly 1 million refugees in Ethiopia risk limited assistance due unprecedented funding crisis](/unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/nearly-1-million-refugees-ethiopia-risk-limited-assistance-due-unprecedented)** | UNHCR Africa | 2024-04-15 | UNHCR warned that healthcare, education, and water gaps were directly affecting refugee lives, with assistance at risk from funding shortfalls. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`
- **[Ethiopia: Mass arbitrary detentions in Amhara region deepen erosion of rule of law](/amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/10/ethiopia-mass-arbitrary-detentions-in-amhara-region-deepen-erosion-of-rule-of-law/)** | Amnesty International | 2024-10-01 | Mass detentions under emergency rule point to coercive control rather than a welfare-first approach to vulnerable populations. | `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.9`
- **[WASH - Gap Analysis for Refugees](/data.unhcr.org/en/documents/details/107435)** | UNHCR | 2024-03-21 | Refugees were receiving about 14 liters of water per person per day, below the 20-liter minimum standard, showing incomplete WASH access. | `6B.3`, `6B.2`

**Search Gap**
- Direct evidence that Abiy personally prioritized disabled people, minorities, or marginalized groups in a sustained, across-the-board way is thin.
- The strongest positives are partner/program documents and reconstruction projects, not a clear national pattern of equal service access.
- The strongest negatives are conflict-driven: civilians, refugees, aid recipients, and residents of Amhara were exposed to violence, access cuts, and emergency coercion, which undercuts any claim of broad prioritization.
